method: Three actually inspected ordinary exterior and aerial pictures, with current standard PMTiles; no bespoke archival or survey research.

references.observed: Actually inspected red-brick twin square gatehouse towers, lower central crenellated bridge, large pointed entrance with closed timber gates and separate small side door, stone quoins/bands and mullioned windows. Original simplified details will omit heraldry and inscriptions. Trees partly hide the right tower.

Actually inspected whole oblique aerial. An open round forecourt is enclosed by warm stone crenellated residential ranges, red-brick tower/hall groups and slate-roofed lower returns. The long hall has tall repeated windows, roof dormers and a small roof lantern. A separate stone church/Garden Museum stands beside the southern gatehouse; detached modern library and garden structures remain separate candidates for native context. Slate hips, stepped flat leads, chimneys, pinnacles and turrets define the varied historic ensemble.

Actually inspected warm pale-stone residential facade with paired slender polygonal corner turrets, battlements, tall mullioned windows, projecting entrance oriel, a closed pointed door and connected lower ranges. Plain original trim will replace heraldry and inscriptions; this crop does not establish the whole rear facade.
